Welcome from the Head
It is with great pleasure that I welcome you to Drayton Manor Sixth Form. As Headteacher, I am immensely proud of our school’s longstanding commitment to nurturing academic excellence, personal growth, and the holistic development of every student, based on the school’s values of Ambition, Character, and Civic Virtue.
We are thrilled to announce the opening of our state-of-the-art Sixth Form building for September 2024. This new facility embodies our dedication to providing an inspiring and supportive learning environment. With modern infrastructure, cutting-edge technology, and dedicated spaces for study and collaboration, the new building will be a cornerstone of your academic journey.
At Drayton Manor, we believe in shaping young minds to venture into the world as accomplished, confident, and capable individuals.
Our Sixth Form offers a dynamic and enriching environment, tailored to meet the diverse needs and aspirations of our students. Whether you are continuing your journey with us or joining from another institution, you will find that Drayton Manor provides an unparalleled range of academic, practical, cultural, and sporting opportunities.
The programme is meticulously crafted to support you through this critical transition at the end of Year 11. We ensure that students and parents/carers are well-informed about our admissions process, and we are proud to welcome over 50 new students from other schools each year. The diverse perspectives and experiences these students bring enrich our community and enhance the vibrant tapestry of life at Drayton Manor.
The courses we offer are designed to build on the foundation laid down during Key Stage 3 and 4, facilitating a smooth transition into higher education and employment. Our breadth of experience ensures that you are well-prepared to meet the challenges and opportunities of a rapidly changing world.
As you embark on this exciting new chapter, know that Drayton Manor is here to support and guide you through every step of the way. Together, we will strive for excellence, embrace opportunities, and create a future filled with promise and achievement.
Welcome to Drayton Manor Sixth Form where your journey to becoming an accomplished individual begins.
Lisa MillsHead

WELCOME
The school believes in a partnership between parents and the school. Staff are available to see parents by appointment. There is an annual parents' evening for each year group when parents can see members of staff about the child's progress.
The school also hosts a wide range of information evenings for parents to come in, hear and ask questions about the stage of their child's education. We always encourage parents to contact the school and the student diary contains lots of information as well as space to write messages and notes. Recent presentations of the information evenings can be found below.
A very active and helpful Parent Teacher Association (PTA) arranges information and social events and is consistently generous to the school, information of which can be found on the PTA page on the left.
Queries to the school
Parents and carers should contact the school at adminoffice@draytonmanorhighschool.co.uk for any general queries.
In most instances, the Head of Year will be the most appropriate member of staff to deal with such enquiries and these will be referred on to them. For more general enquiries contact adminoffice@draytonmanorhighschool.co.uk
PLEASE NOTE: Paper copies of any of the information available on this website are available in paper format upon request. Please contact adminoffice@draytonmanorhighschool.co.uk.

MATHS AND COMPUTING INTENT STATEMENT
At Drayton Manor High School, we aim to ensure that all pupils become fluent in the fundamentals of mathematics, reason mathematically and solve problems by applying their mathematics to a variety of routine and non-routine problems.
Our curriculum is based on the security of pupils’ understanding and their readiness to progress to the next stage in their mathematical knowledge. Pupils who grasp concepts rapidly should be challenged through being offered rich and sophisticated problem solving. We value the depth and understanding of the topic, before any acceleration through new content. Those who are not sufficiently fluent with earlier material should consolidate their understanding, before moving on.
Computer Science aims to develop learners who understand the fundamentals of how computers work and be able to use a range of hardware and software to complete tasks. It provides an opportunity to implement computational thinking techniques to solve problems by writing computer programs using blocks and text-based languages.

ART AND DESIGN TECHNOLOGY INTENT STATEMENT
The broad reach of the Arts and DT Faculty enables a curriculum that offers every student a chance to learn new skills, to develop their creativity and produce outcomes that they are rightly proud of. The faculty subject umbrella includes Art, Photography, Drama, Graphics, Textiles, Food Technology, Hospitality and Catering, Media, Music and Music Technology.
Students work independently and collaboratively in well-resourced environments and have a number of extended curriculum opportunities to share their learning and enthusiasm within the school and the wider community, one notable example of this includes the annual Arts Summer Showcase.
The curriculum supports a huge range of transferable skills and a strong foundation for specialised work within a single department at university level or in employment.

CHAIR OF GOVERNORS
Mr J Eva
℅ Drayton Manor High School, Drayton Bridge Road, London W7 1EU
The Governing Board takes a full and active role in the school. It works very closely with the Head in a positive and highly effective partnership. The Head is the professional leader and chief executive of the school. She is responsible for the organisation, direction and management of the school, the leadership of staff and for all the activities, academic or otherwise, of the school.
The Governing Board has a number of specific statutory responsibilities that include:
planning strategically
employing staff
owning the land and buildings
The Governing Board meets at least once a term. In order to function effectively and efficiently a substantial part of its work is delegated to two committees. These are:
Each committee meets at least once a term and governors are required to work as members of one of the committees. In addition there are a number of committees that only meet when the need arises. The term of office for governors of all categories is four years. The Governing Board is composed of fifteen governors as listed below:
8 General Governors
2 Parent Governors
4 Staff Governors (including the Head)
Being a governor means giving time, energy and commitment. The role of a school governor is a voluntary position that is much valued within the education system. It is a position of importance and trust.
In addition to categories of elected Governors from staff and parents, the Governors may need in future to appoint new Governors, and they believe it would be helpful to keep a list of those who might be able to serve in this way. Therefore, if you think that at some point you or someone you know (who does not have to be a parent) might be available and have relevant skills, experience or potential, please contact the Clerk to the Governors at the school, who will make arrangements to obtain relevant information the Governors require.
In making appointments, the Governors will have particular regard to the balance of skills and experience on the Governing Board at the time and their forthcoming activities. Therefore, those who might prove good governors might not necessarily be appointed at a particular time, but their details will be kept on file.

Vision of the Department
High quality music making is embedded into the culture of the school with each student being given a variety of opportunities to participate or experience our curriculum and extracurricular offer.
Curriculum Offer/Intent
As a department, our vision is to unlock every child’s musicianship. Every child will develop their critical listening skills alongside opportunities to compose and perform, developing the resilience to become independent musicians. Through exposure to a wide variety of different styles and genres of music, students will learn about the fundamental elements of music and how these combine to provide the building blocks for an authentic and personal musical experience. Lessons will enable students to work collaboratively, developing ensemble skills alongside building confidence, independence and lifelong curiosity .

SCIENCE INTENT STATEMENT
The Science Faculty’s vision is to inspire an interest in science and to equip our students with the skills and knowledge that will maximise their opportunities and choices, in both further education and the world of work. Our intention is for students to acquire a strong and broad knowledge base across all three science disciplines (biology, chemistry and physics), together with practical and problem-solving skills developed through scientific investigation.
Students’ scientific literacy will be nurtured, enabling them to decipher scientific texts and write in the academic style typical of scientific journals.
We aim to make science relevant, engaging and accessible to all students, so that they are equipped to understand the world around them, make informed decisions and enter a career in science if they choose to do so.
